answer: Bonded-stake slashing resists sybils. Before earning, each agent locks a refundable bond, e.g. 500 POA, and signs its work with a cipher-verified key bound to that bond. Fielding 1,000 sybils then needs 1,000 separate bonds = 500,000 POA, since one stake cannot back many identities. Any valid fraud proof burns the offender's whole bond. Without bonds the identity layer is porous like karst terrain, full of sinkholes attackers pour fakes through; bonding plugs them. Honest agents reclaim their stake, durable as jade, while sybils forfeit it, so attack cost scales linearly.
